environment.description: Same Ktor microservice deployed on RHEL 9 with a custom SELinux type enforcement policy (authsvc_t). The policy module defines a narrow file context: only /opt/app/config/** is labeled authsvc_conf_t and readable by the process domain. The key file at /opt/app/keys/public.pem is labeled authsvc_key_t with a type_transition rule that restricts read access to a separate domain (keymgr_t) used only during initial key loading at systemd service start via a oneshot ExecStartPre unit. After the service enters authsvc_t domain via automatic transition on the main binary, the process CANNOT re-read /opt/app/keys/public.pem because authsvc_t lacks 'read' permission on authsvc_key_t labeled files. The cachedPublicKey is populated during the ExecStartPre phase and passed via a Unix domain socket to the main process. If the cache is invalidated or the application attempts to re-read the key file (as happens when cachedPublicKey is null on a new code path), the SELinux policy returns EACCES. The HMAC algorithm paths in buildVerifier() call loadPublicKey() which attempts file I/O that is denied by the MAC policy, causing the catch block to return null and reject the forged token.

config.cache_behavior: cachedPublicKey populated via IPC from keymgr, not direct file read
deny_rules: deny authsvc_t authsvc_key_t:file { read open getattr }
